audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Lucian five of the seven stages while every prose block on the same page says Kled takes over from level 2 onward. The packet chart and the already-audited mirror both read Lucian, Kled, Kled, Kled, Kled, Kled, Skill. diff was 'HARD' but diffRating was 5.5/10, tone was the yellow even-colour, and both rating lines read 'Even matchup'.
audit.why: Lucian's 43.88% here is a losing lane. Kled's grab plus Jousting plus the remount shield beat a marksman's HP bar from level 2; only level 1, before he has a grab, is Lucian's.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 set to Kled and row 6 to Skill in both layers as matched pairs, ratings re-scaled to 3/2/3/3/2/5. diffRating raised to 7.5/10, carryRating to 7/10, tone moved to the orange #ff8b3d, and both rating lines reworded to 'Hard matchup' so the label, the colour and the number finally agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] described level 6 as Lucian's spike; on this lane 6 is Kled's. No cooldown numbers appeared anywhere in the chart.
audit.why: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110s at 3500-4500 range with a shield, and it remounts him mid-fight. The Culling is only damage.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Chaaaaaaaarge!!! and its 140s rank-1 cooldown; Bear Trap's 800 range and 11s cooldown added to the interactions row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Violent Tendencies was described as 'sustain' and never as what it is — an attack-speed burst of four attacks with a heavier fourth, flagged in missingInteractions as the burst tell.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Kled gains massive attack speed for four attacks. The fourth attack deals more damage.' The wind-up on the first of those four is the cue to leave, not the cast; a player waiting for a cast animation eats all four.
audit.corrected: The four-attack pattern and the heavier fourth written into dontsFull[0].d; the auto-reset tell into report[5].t.
sources: enemyKit Kled W text and autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'Violent Tendencies' in whys[3] as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: Violent Tendencies is the real Riot name of Kled's W — the kit file confirms it. False positive in suspectNames.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Kled carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Kled carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Kled carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: E online — dash-weave trades start now: spell, double-shot, dash out before his answer lands.
edits.after: Kled spikes the moment he can grab and dismount-charge — his skirmish power beats your level 2.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-AA-E-AA-W-AA strings chunk a third of his HP. Trade on every CS he takes from the wrong angle.
edits.after: Grab, Jousting and remount stacking online — Q-W-E lets you survive a mounted Kled, not beat him.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Bear Trap on a Rope — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies sustain and remount restacking out-trade you in any extended fight, and your mana strains first.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! crosses the wave on 140s and remounts him mid-fight — your R is only damage.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: His first bruiser item plus the remount HP pool outpaces your first-item peak unless you already snowballed.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: Even by two items only if you converted early — a hard-scaling Kled reclaims it with raw stats otherwise.

edits.before: Track Kled’s Bear Trap on a Rope: The hook starts his all-in — dodge it and disengage his remount. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Bear Trap on a Rope is 800 range on 11s — dodge it and his all-in stalls. Violent Tendencies is an auto reset: the wind-up is your cue, not the cast.

edits.before: Kled whiffs Bear Trap on a Rope and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Ardent Blaze marks him — the move speed keeps you outside Jousting's 550.

edits.before: That is Kled’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies gives four fast attacks and the fourth hits hardest — leave first.

notes: The mirror's note calls this the worst two-layer disagreement in its slice, and it is: the page rendered Lucian winning five stages at 8/10 each while its own early/mid/late prose said Kled takes over at 2. Both layers agreed with each other, so the existing pair-check would not have caught it — only the prose did. The tone/diffRating/label triple was also internally inconsistent (diff HARD, yellow even-colour, 'Even matchup' text) and is now aligned.
